P1● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

A toy is a hemisphere of diameter 14 cm with a cone on top. The curved surface area of its hemispherical part is: (Use π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​.)

CSA of a hemisphere =2πr2= 2\pi r^2=2πr2 (Topic 1). Why it applies: only the curved part is asked.

2πr22\pi r^22πr2 with r=7r = 7r=7 cm.
This uses the diameter 14 cm as the radius.
This is 3πr23\pi r^23πr2 — it adds the flat face, which is hidden under the cone.
This is 4πr24\pi r^24πr2, a whole sphere.

Given: diameter 14 cm, so r=7r = 7r=7 cm. Asked: the CSA of the hemisphere.

Concept used: CSA of a hemisphere =2πr2= 2\pi r^2=2πr2 (Topic 1). Why it applies: only the curved part is asked.

  1. Hidden faces: the hemisphere's flat face is under the cone — it is not part of the curved surface in any case.

  2. 1

    r=142=7r = \dfrac{14}{2} = 7r=214​=7 cm.

  3. 2

    CSA =2×227×7×7=308= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 308=2×722​×7×7=308 cm².

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ 2πr22\pi r^22πr2 with r=7r = 7r=7 cm.
    • (b) ✘ This uses the diameter 14 cm as the radius.
    • (c) ✘ This is 3πr23\pi r^23πr2 — it adds the flat face, which is hidden under the cone.
    • (d) ✘ This is 4πr24\pi r^24πr2, a whole sphere.

  4. Check: a whole sphere of radius 7 cm has 4×154=6164 \times 154 = 6164×154=616 cm², and half of it is 308 cm² ✔.

  5. Answer (a)

    Common trap: Forgetting to halve the diameter.
P2● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

A cube of edge 6 cm is glued to the middle of the top face of a cube of edge 10 cm. The total surface area of the solid is: (π is not needed here.)

TSA = sum of the TSAs − the two hidden faces (Topic 2). Why it applies: the small cube's base presses on a square of the big cube's top.

This adds the two TSAs — the hidden faces are counted.
This takes away only one of the two hidden squares.
Both hidden squares are taken away.
This is the big cube alone.

Given: cubes of edge 10 cm and 6 cm. Asked: the TSA of the solid.

Concept used: TSA = sum of the TSAs − the two hidden faces (Topic 2). Why it applies: the small cube's base presses on a square of the big cube's top.

  1. Hidden faces: the small cube's base (36 cm²) and the 6 cm × 6 cm square of the big cube's top under it (36 cm²).

  2. 1

    Big cube =6×100=600= 6 \times 100 = 600=6×100=600 cm²; small cube =6×36=216= 6 \times 36 = 216=6×36=216 cm².

  3. 2

    TSA =600+216−36−36=744= 600 + 216 - 36 - 36 = 744=600+216−36−36=744 cm².

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (c) ✔ Both hidden squares are taken away.
    • (a) ✘ This adds the two TSAs — the hidden faces are counted.
    • (b) ✘ This takes away only one of the two hidden squares.
    • (d) ✘ This is the big cube alone.

  4. Check: the small cube adds only its 4 side faces to the outside: 600+4×36=744600 + 4 \times 36 = 744600+4×36=744 cm² ✔.

  5. Answer (c)

    Common trap: Taking away only the small cube's base — the square it covers on the big cube is hidden too.
P3● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

A cuboidal block 12 cm × 9 cm × 7 cm has a cylindrical hole of radius 2 cm and depth 2.5 cm drilled into its top face (not right through). Find the total surface area of the block. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: cuboid 12 × 9 × 7 (cm); hole r=2r = 2r=2 cm, depth 2.5 cm. Asked: the TSA.

Concept used: TSA of cuboid − opening + wall of the hole + bottom of the hole (Topic 3). Why it applies: the hole removes a circle and adds its own wall and bottom.

  1. Hidden faces: the circle of radius 2 cm in the top face is gone; the hole's wall and its flat bottom are new surface.

  2. 1

    TSA of cuboid =2(12×9+9×7+7×12)=2(108+63+84)=510= 2(12 \times 9 + 9 \times 7 + 7 \times 12) = 2(108 + 63 + 84) = 510=2(12×9+9×7+7×12)=2(108+63+84)=510 cm².

  3. 2

    Opening =3.14×2×2=12.56= 3.14 \times 2 \times 2 = 12.56=3.14×2×2=12.56 cm² (gone); bottom of the hole =12.56= 12.56=12.56 cm² (new).

  4. 3

    Wall =2×3.14×2×2.5=31.4= 2 \times 3.14 \times 2 \times 2.5 = 31.4=2×3.14×2×2.5=31.4 cm² (new).

  5. 4

    TSA =510−12.56+31.4+12.56=541.4= 510 - 12.56 + 31.4 + 12.56 = 541.4=510−12.56+31.4+12.56=541.4 cm².

  6. Check: a hole that does not go through changes the surface by its wall only (its bottom replaces its opening): 510+31.4=541.4510 + 31.4 = 541.4510+31.4=541.4 cm² ✔.

  7. Answer 541.4 cm²

    Common trap: Subtracting the opening and the wall (that gives 466.04 cm²) — the inside of the hole is part of the surface.

P4● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

A solid is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. Its total length is 20 cm and its radius is 4 cm. Find (a) the length of the cylindrical part and (b) the surface area of the solid. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: total length 20 cm; r=4r = 4r=4 cm. Asked: the cylinder's length; the surface area.

Concept used: cylinder length =L−2r= L - 2r=L−2r; surface = CSA of cylinder + 4πr24\pi r^24πr2 (Topic 2). Why it applies: each hemisphere takes up 4 cm of the length.

  1. Hidden faces: the two ends of the cylinder and the flat faces of the two hemispheres.

  2. 1

    (a) Cylinder length =20−2×4=12= 20 - 2 \times 4 = 12=20−2×4=12 cm.

  3. 2

    (b) CSA of cylinder =2×3.14×4×12=301.44= 2 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 12 = 301.44=2×3.14×4×12=301.44 cm².

  4. 3

    Two hemispheres =4×3.14×4×4=200.96= 4 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 4 = 200.96=4×3.14×4×4=200.96 cm².

  5. 4

    Surface =301.44+200.96=502.4= 301.44 + 200.96 = 502.4=301.44+200.96=502.4 cm².

  6. Check: 2πr×L=2×3.14×4×20=502.42\pi r \times L = 2 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 20 = 502.42πr×L=2×3.14×4×20=502.4 cm² ✔.

  7. Answer (a) 12 cm (b) 502.4 cm²

    Common trap: Using 20 cm for the cylinder and adding the hemispheres — that gives 703.36 cm².

This is the cone's volume, 13π×81×12\dfrac{1}{3}\pi \times 81 \times 1231​π×81×12, in cm³.

    • (c) ✘ This is the hemisphere's CSA, 2π×812\pi \times 812π×81.

P6● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

(a) A hemispherical dome on a temple has radius 5 m. Find the area of its outside surface (the curved part only). (b) A solid hemispherical paperweight has radius 5 cm. Find its total surface area. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: (a) dome r=5r = 5r=5 m; (b) solid hemisphere r=5r = 5r=5 cm. Asked: the dome's curved surface; the paperweight's TSA.

Concept used: CSA of a hemisphere 2πr22\pi r^22πr2; TSA of a solid hemisphere 3πr23\pi r^23πr2 (Topic 1). Why it applies: the dome's flat face sits on the building (hidden); the paperweight's flat face is on the outside.

  1. Hidden faces: (a) the dome's flat face is joined to the top of the building.

  2. 1

    (a) 2×3.14×5×5=1572 \times 3.14 \times 5 \times 5 = 1572×3.14×5×5=157 m².

  3. 2

    (b) 3×3.14×5×5=235.53 \times 3.14 \times 5 \times 5 = 235.53×3.14×5×5=235.5 cm².

  4. Check: (b) − (a) in numbers is one circle: 235.5−157=78.5=3.14×25235.5 - 157 = 78.5 = 3.14 \times 25235.5−157=78.5=3.14×25 ✔.

  5. Answer (a) 157 m² (b) 235.5 cm²

    Common trap: Using 4πr24\pi r^24πr2 (a sphere) for either, or 2πr22\pi r^22πr2 for the solid paperweight.

volume = cylinder + hemisphere; 1 m³ = 1000 litres (Topic 4). Why it applies: the water fills both parts.

This multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.
m³ × 1000.
This multiplies by 10 000.
This is the number of cm³, not of litres.

Given: r=70r = 70r=70 cm =0.7= 0.7=0.7 m; cylinder height 1.5 m. Asked: the capacity in litres.

Concept used: volume = cylinder + hemisphere; 1 m³ = 1000 litres (Topic 4). Why it applies: the water fills both parts.

  1. Hidden faces: the cylinder's bottom and the hemisphere's flat face are joined (one open space); the volumes add.

  2. 1

    Use metres: r=0.7r = 0.7r=0.7 m.

  3. 2

    Cylinder =227×0.7×0.7×1.5=2.31= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0.7 \times 0.7 \times 1.5 = 2.31=722​×0.7×0.7×1.5=2.31 m³.

  4. 3

    Hemisphere =23×227×0.7×0.7×0.7=2.1563≈0.7187= \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 0.7 \times 0.7 \times 0.7 = \dfrac{2.156}{3} \approx 0.7187=32​×722​×0.7×0.7×0.7=32.156​≈0.7187 m³.

  5. 4

    Total ≈3.0287\approx 3.0287≈3.0287 m³ =3028.67= 3028.67=3028.67 litres.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (b) ✔ m³ × 1000.
    • (a) ✘ This multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.
    • (c) ✘ This multiplies by 10 000.
    • (d) ✘ This is the number of cm³, not of litres.

  6. Check: in cm: cylinder 154×10×10×150=2 310 000154 \times 10 \times 10 \times 150 = 2\,310\,000154×10×10×150=2310000 cm³ =2310= 2310=2310 litres, and the hemisphere ≈718.67\approx 718.67≈718.67 litres; 2310+718.67=3028.672310 + 718.67 = 3028.672310+718.67=3028.67 ✔.

    Common trap: Mixing 70 cm with 1.5 m in one formula.
P8● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

A cylindrical wooden log has radius 7 cm and length 20 cm. A cone of the same radius and height 9 cm is hollowed out of one end. Find the volume of wood left. (Use π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​.)

Full solution

Given: cylinder r=7r = 7r=7 cm, h=20h = 20h=20 cm; cone r=7r = 7r=7 cm, h=9h = 9h=9 cm. Asked: the wood left.

Concept used: wood left = cylinder − cone (Topic 4). Why it applies: the hollow removes a cone of wood.

  1. Hidden faces: the end circle of the log is cut away by the cone's base; for the volume, the cone of wood is removed.

  2. 1

    Cylinder =227×7×7×20=3080= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 \times 20 = 3080=722​×7×7×20=3080 cm³.

  3. 2

    Cone =13×154×9=462= \dfrac{1}{3} \times 154 \times 9 = 462=31​×154×9=462 cm³.

  4. 3

    Wood left =3080−462=2618= 3080 - 462 = 2618=3080−462=2618 cm³.

  5. Check: 154×(20−3)=154×17=2618154 \times (20 - 3) = 154 \times 17 = 2618154×(20−3)=154×17=2618 cm³ (a cone is a third of a cylinder, so removing it is like losing 93=3\dfrac{9}{3} = 339​=3 cm of length) ✔.

  6. Answer 2618 cm³

    Common trap: Adding the cone (3542 cm³) — a hollow takes wood away.

P9● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

A water tower is a cylinder of radius 3.5 m and height 12 m with a hemispherical dome of the same radius on top. The curved wall and the dome are painted at ₹40 per m². Find the cost. (Use π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​.)

Full solution

Given: r=3.5r = 3.5r=3.5 m; wall 12 m; ₹40 per m². Asked: the cost.

Concept used: painted area = CSA of cylinder + CSA of hemisphere; cost = area × rate (Topic 2). Why it applies: only the outside curved surfaces are painted.

  1. Hidden faces: the cylinder's top and the dome's flat face are joined; the base stands on the ground.

  2. 1

    Wall =2×227×3.5×12=264= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 12 = 264=2×722​×3.5×12=264 m².

  3. 2

    Dome =2×227×3.5×3.5=77= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5 = 77=2×722​×3.5×3.5=77 m².

  4. 3

    Area =264+77=341= 264 + 77 = 341=264+77=341 m²; cost =341×40=13 640= 341 \times 40 = 13\,640=341×40=13640, so ₹13 640.

  5. Check: 2πr(h+r)=22×15.5=3412\pi r(h + r) = 22 \times 15.5 = 3412πr(h+r)=22×15.5=341 m² ✔.

  6. Answer ₹13 640

    Common trap: Painting the dome as 3πr23\pi r^23πr2 — its flat face is hidden on top of the wall.

P10●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

A toy is a cone on a hemisphere. The diameter of the toy is 16 cm and its total height is 14 cm. Find the total surface area of the toy. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: diameter 16 cm, so r=8r = 8r=8 cm; total height 14 cm. Asked: the TSA.

Concept used: TSA = CSA of cone + CSA of hemisphere; cone height = total − r (Topic 2). Why it applies: the hemisphere's radius is part of the height.

  1. Hidden faces: the cone's base and the hemisphere's flat face are glued together.

  2. 1

    r=8r = 8r=8 cm; cone height =14−8=6= 14 - 8 = 6=14−8=6 cm.

  3. 2

    l=82+62=10l = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10l=82+62​=10 cm.

  4. 3

    CSA of cone =π×8×10=80π= \pi \times 8 \times 10 = 80\pi=π×8×10=80π cm²; CSA of hemisphere =2π×64=128π= 2\pi \times 64 = 128\pi=2π×64=128π cm².

  5. 4

    TSA =208π=208×3.14=653.12= 208\pi = 208 \times 3.14 = 653.12=208π=208×3.14=653.12 cm².

  6. Check: from the two TSAs: π×8×18+3π×64=144π+192π=336π\pi \times 8 \times 18 + 3\pi \times 64 = 144\pi + 192\pi = 336\piπ×8×18+3π×64=144π+192π=336π; less the two hidden circles 2×64π2 \times 64\pi2×64π: 336π−128π=208π336\pi - 128\pi = 208\pi336π−128π=208π ✔.

  7. Answer 653.12 cm²

    Common trap: Using the diameter 16 cm as the radius, or 14 cm as the cone's height.

P11●● StandardShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

Two identical solid cones, each of radius 5 cm and height 12 cm, are joined base to base. Find the surface area of the solid formed. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: two cones, r=5r = 5r=5 cm, h=12h = 12h=12 cm. Asked: the surface area.

Concept used: surface = 2 × CSA of a cone (Topic 2). Why it applies: the bases are pressed together.

  1. Hidden faces: both circular bases.

  2. 1

    l=52+122=13l = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = 13l=52+122​=13 cm.

  3. 2

    Surface =2×π×5×13=130π=130×3.14=408.2= 2 \times \pi \times 5 \times 13 = 130\pi = 130 \times 3.14 = 408.2=2×π×5×13=130π=130×3.14=408.2 cm².

  4. Check: from the TSAs: 2×π×5×(13+5)=180π2 \times \pi \times 5 \times (13 + 5) = 180\pi2×π×5×(13+5)=180π; less two bases 50π50\pi50π: 130π130\pi130π ✔.

  5. Answer 408.2 cm²

    Common trap: Doubling the TSA of one cone (565.2 cm²) — the bases are inside.

P12●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

A solid cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 10 cm has a hemisphere of radius 6 cm scooped out of its top face. Find the total surface area of the remaining solid. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: r=6r = 6r=6 cm; h=10h = 10h=10 cm; hollow radius 6 cm. Asked: the TSA.

Concept used: CSA of cylinder + bottom + inner surface of the hollow (Topic 3). Why it applies: the whole top circle is cut away and replaced by the hollow.

  1. Hidden faces: the top circle of the cylinder is cut away; the hollow adds 2πr22\pi r^22πr2.

  2. 1

    CSA of cylinder =2π×6×10=120π= 2\pi \times 6 \times 10 = 120\pi=2π×6×10=120π cm².

  3. 2

    Bottom =36π= 36\pi=36π cm²; hollow =2π×36=72π= 2\pi \times 36 = 72\pi=2π×36=72π cm².

  4. 3

    TSA =120π+36π+72π=228π=228×3.14=715.92= 120\pi + 36\pi + 72\pi = 228\pi = 228 \times 3.14 = 715.92=120π+36π+72π=228π=228×3.14=715.92 cm².

  5. Check: from the full cylinder: 2π×6×16=192π2\pi \times 6 \times 16 = 192\pi2π×6×16=192π, and the change is +πr2=36π+\pi r^2 = 36\pi+πr2=36π: 228π228\pi228π ✔.

  6. Answer 715.92 cm²

    Common trap: Keeping the top circle as well as the hollow (that gives 828.96 cm²).

P13●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

A tent is a cylinder of radius 6 m with a conical top. The wall is 3 m high and the total height of the tent is 11 m. Find the area of canvas needed for the wall and the roof. (Use π = 3.14.)

Full solution

Given: r=6r = 6r=6 m; wall 3 m; total height 11 m. Asked: the canvas.

Concept used: canvas = CSA of cylinder + CSA of cone; cone height = total − wall (Topic 2). Why it applies: the floor has no canvas.

  1. Hidden faces: the cone's base and the cylinder's top are joined; the floor is not covered.

  2. 1

    Cone height =11−3=8= 11 - 3 = 8=11−3=8 m; l=62+82=10l = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10l=62+82​=10 m.

  3. 2

    Wall =2π×6×3=36π= 2\pi \times 6 \times 3 = 36\pi=2π×6×3=36π m²; roof =π×6×10=60π= \pi \times 6 \times 10 = 60\pi=π×6×10=60π m².

  4. 3

    Canvas =96π=96×3.14=301.44= 96\pi = 96 \times 3.14 = 301.44=96π=96×3.14=301.44 m².

  5. Check: πr(2h+l)=6π×(6+10)=96π\pi r(2h + l) = 6\pi \times (6 + 10) = 96\piπr(2h+l)=6π×(6+10)=96π ✔.

  6. Answer 301.44 m²

    Common trap: Taking 11 m as the cone's height — the wall is part of the total height.

    Cone height =132−52=144=12= \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12=132−52​=144​=12 cm.

    Cone =13π×25×12=100π= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi \times 25 \times 12 = 100\pi=31​π×25×12=100π cm³.

    Cylinder =π×25×11=275π= \pi \times 25 \times 11 = 275\pi=π×25×11=275π cm³.

    Volume =375π=375×3.14=1177.5= 375\pi = 375 \times 3.14 = 1177.5=375π=375×3.14=1177.5 cm³.

  7. Answer 1177.5 cm³

    Common trap: Using 13 cm as the cone's height (about 1203.67 cm³).

P15●● StandardMCQ · 1 markOriginal

Two solid hemispheres, each of radius 7 cm, are joined along their flat faces. The total surface area of the new solid is: (Use π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​.)

the solid is a sphere: 4πr24\pi r^24πr2 (Topic 2). Why it applies: the two flat faces are pressed together.

This is 2×3πr22 \times 3\pi r^22×3πr2 — both hidden flat faces are counted.
This is one curved surface only.
Two curved surfaces, a sphere.
This takes each hemisphere as a whole sphere, 2×4πr22 \times 4\pi r^22×4πr2.

Given: two hemispheres, r=7r = 7r=7 cm. Asked: the TSA of the solid.

Concept used: the solid is a sphere: 4πr24\pi r^24πr2 (Topic 2). Why it applies: the two flat faces are pressed together.

  1. Hidden faces: both flat faces.

  2. 1

    TSA =2×2πr2=4×227×7×7=616= 2 \times 2\pi r^2 = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 616=2×2πr2=4×722​×7×7=616 cm².

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (c) ✔ Two curved surfaces, a sphere.
    • (a) ✘ This is 2×3πr22 \times 3\pi r^22×3πr2 — both hidden flat faces are counted.
    • (b) ✘ This is one curved surface only.

P23●● StandardAssertion–Reason · 1 markOriginal
AWhen two solids are joined, the volume of the new solid is the sum of their volumes.
RWhen two solids are joined, the surface area of the new solid is the sum of their surface areas.
joined faces hide surface but not space (Topics 2 and 4). Why it applies: both statements are about joining solids.

Given: A and R. Asked: the correct option.

Concept used: joined faces hide surface but not space (Topics 2 and 4). Why it applies: both statements are about joining solids.

  1. Hidden faces: in any joined solid, the two faces pressed together are hidden — they leave the surface, but no space is lost.

  2. 1

    A: no space disappears when solids are joined, so the volumes add — true.

  3. 2

    R: the two joined faces are no longer on the outside, so the surface is less than the sum — false.

  4. Check: two cubes of edge 1 cm: volume 1+1=21 + 1 = 21+1=2 cm³ ✔ (A); surface 101010 cm², not 6+6=126 + 6 = 126+6=12 cm² (R fails) ✔.

  5. Answer (C)

    Common trap: Thinking surfaces add like volumes — that is the commonest mistake in this chapter.

  1. Hidden faces: the cone's open top and the hemisphere's flat face are joined; the volumes add.

    (i) l=3.52+8.42=12.25+70.56=82.81=9.1l = \sqrt{3.5^2 + 8.4^2} = \sqrt{12.25 + 70.56} = \sqrt{82.81} = 9.1l=3.52+8.42​=12.25+70.56​=82.81​=9.1 cm.

    (ii) Cone =13×227×3.5×3.5×8.4=107.8= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5 \times 8.4 = 107.8=31​×722​×3.5×3.5×8.4=107.8 cm³; hemisphere =5396= \dfrac{539}{6}=6539​ cm³; one serving =107.8+5396=1185.86≈197.63= 107.8 + \dfrac{539}{6} = \dfrac{1185.8}{6} \approx 197.63=107.8+6539​=61185.8​≈197.63 cm³.

  4. 3

    (iii) (A) 60×1185.86=11 85860 \times \dfrac{1185.8}{6} = 11\,85860×61185.8​=11858 cm³ =11.858= 11.858=11.858 litres.

  5. 4

    (iii) (B) One wafer =227×3.5×9.1=100.1= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 9.1 = 100.1=722​×3.5×9.1=100.1 cm²; 60 wafers =6006= 6006=6006 cm².

  6. Check: (i) 9.12=82.81=3.52+8.429.1^2 = 82.81 = 3.5^2 + 8.4^29.12=82.81=3.52+8.42 ✔; (iii) (A) 10×1185.8=11 85810 \times 1185.8 = 11\,85810×1185.8=11858 ✔ (60 ÷ 6 = 10); (iii) (B) 11×9.1=100.111 \times 9.1 = 100.111×9.1=100.1 ✔ (227×3.5=11\dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5 = 11722​×3.5=11).

  7. Answer (i) 9.1 cm (ii) about 197.63 cm³ (iii) (A) 11.858 litres (B) 6006 cm²

A storage tank is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. Its total length is 7 m and its diameter is 2.8 m. Find (a) how many litres it holds, to two decimal places, and (b) the cost of painting its outside at ₹45 per m². (Use π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​.)

Full solution

Given: total length 7 m; r=1.4r = 1.4r=1.4 m; ₹45 per m². Asked: the capacity; the cost.

Concept used: (a) cylinder (length 7−2.8=4.27 - 2.8 = 4.27−2.8=4.2 m) + a sphere; (b) surface =2πr×= 2\pi r \times=2πr× total length (Topics 2, 4). Why it applies: the tank is a capsule shape.

  1. Hidden faces: the cylinder's two ends and the hemispheres' flat faces are joined in pairs.

  2. 1

    (a) Cylinder =227×1.4×1.4×4.2=6.16×4.2=25.872= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 1.4 \times 1.4 \times 4.2 = 6.16 \times 4.2 = 25.872=722​×1.4×1.4×4.2=6.16×4.2=25.872 m³.

  3. 2

    Two hemispheres =43×227×1.4×1.4×1.4=34.4963≈11.4987= \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 1.4 \times 1.4 \times 1.4 = \dfrac{34.496}{3} \approx 11.4987=34​×722​×1.4×1.4×1.4=334.496​≈11.4987 m³.

  4. 3

    Capacity =25.872+34.4963=112.1123≈37.3707= 25.872 + \dfrac{34.496}{3} = \dfrac{112.112}{3} \approx 37.3707=25.872+334.496​=3112.112​≈37.3707 m³ ≈37 370.67\approx 37\,370.67≈37370.67 litres.

    (b) Surface =2×227×1.4×4.2+4×227×1.4×1.4=36.96+24.64=61.6= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 1.4 \times 4.2 + 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 1.4 \times 1.4 = 36.96 + 24.64 = 61.6=2×722​×1.4×4.2+4×722​×1.4×1.4=36.96+24.64=61.6 m².

P30●●● AdvancedLong answer · 5 marksOriginal

A solid cylinder of radius r and height h (with h>rh > rh>r) has a hemisphere of radius r stuck on one end and a hemisphere of radius r scooped out of the other end.
(a) Show that the volume of the solid is πr2h\pi r^2 hπr2h and its total surface area is 2πr(h+2r)2\pi r(h + 2r)2πr(h+2r).
(b) Find both for r=2.1r = 2.1r=2.1 cm and h=6h = 6h=6 cm. (Use π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​.)

Full solution

Given: cylinder r, h; a hemisphere added at one end, one removed at the other. Asked: general formulas; values.

Concept used: volumes add for the stuck-on part and subtract for the scooped-out part; each end's surface changes by +πr2+\pi r^2+πr2 (Topics 3, 4). Why it applies: the same hemisphere is added once and removed once.

  1. Hidden faces: at the top, the hemisphere's flat face and the cylinder's top are joined; at the bottom, the bottom circle is cut away and the hollow's inside is new.

  2. 1

    (a) Volume =πr2h+23πr3−23πr3=πr2h= \pi r^2 h + \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3 - \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \pi r^2 h=πr2h+32​πr3−32​πr3=πr2h.

  3. 2

    Surface: CSA of cylinder 2πrh2\pi r h2πrh + dome outside 2πr22\pi r^22πr2 + hollow inside 2πr22\pi r^22πr2 =2πrh+4πr2=2πr(h+2r)= 2\pi r h + 4\pi r^2 = 2\pi r(h + 2r)=2πrh+4πr2=2πr(h+2r).

  4. 3

    (b) Volume =227×2.1×2.1×6=13.86×6=83.16= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2.1 \times 2.1 \times 6 = 13.86 \times 6 = 83.16=722​×2.1×2.1×6=13.86×6=83.16 cm³.

  5. 4

    Surface =2×227×2.1×(6+4.2)=13.2×10.2=134.64= 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 2.1 \times (6 + 4.2) = 13.2 \times 10.2 = 134.64=2×722​×2.1×(6+4.2)=13.2×10.2=134.64 cm².

  6. Check: the surface also equals the cylinder's TSA plus πr2\pi r^2πr2 at each end: 2πr(r+h)+2πr2=13.2×8.1+27.72=106.92+27.72=134.642\pi r(r + h) + 2\pi r^2 = 13.2 \times 8.1 + 27.72 = 106.92 + 27.72 = 134.642πr(r+h)+2πr2=13.2×8.1+27.72=106.92+27.72=134.64 cm² ✔.

  7. Answer (b) 83.16 cm³; 134.64 cm²

    Common trap: Thinking the scooped end lowers the surface. Like the stuck-on end, it raises it by πr2\pi r^2πr2.

    Ice cream =56×125π=625π6=6256×227≈327.38= \dfrac{5}{6} \times 125\pi = \dfrac{625\pi}{6} = \dfrac{625}{6} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \approx 327.38=65​×125π=6625π​=6625​×722​≈327.38 cm³.

E18●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 12, Ex 12.4 Q3

How many cubic centimetres of iron is required to construct an open box whose external dimensions are 36 cm, 25 cm and 16.5 cm provided the thickness of the iron is 1.5 cm. If one cubic cm of iron weighs 7.5 g, find the weight of the box.

π to use: none needed — no circles.

Full solution

Given: outside 36 × 25 × 16.5 (cm); thickness 1.5 cm; open at the top; 7.5 g per cm³. Asked: the iron; the weight.

Concept used: iron = outer cuboid − inner hollow cuboid (Topic 4). Why it applies: the box is a cuboid with a cuboid hollowed out of it.

  1. Hidden faces: none are joined — the box is a cuboid with a smaller cuboid hollowed out of it, open at the top; for the volume, the hollow is subtracted (its height loses only one thickness, as there is no lid).

  2. 1

    Inside: 36−3=3336 - 3 = 3336−3=33 cm, 25−3=2225 - 3 = 2225−3=22 cm, 16.5−1.5=1516.5 - 1.5 = 1516.5−1.5=15 cm.

  3. 2

    Outer =36×25×16.5=14 850= 36 \times 25 \times 16.5 = 14\,850=36×25×16.5=14850 cm³; inner =33×22×15=10 890= 33 \times 22 \times 15 = 10\,890=33×22×15=10890 cm³.

  4. 3

    Iron =14 850−10 890=3960= 14\,850 - 10\,890 = 3960=14850−10890=3960 cm³.

  5. 4

    Weight =3960×7.5=29 700= 3960 \times 7.5 = 29\,700=3960×7.5=29700 g =29.7= 29.7=29.7 kg.

  6. Check: count the iron piece by piece — bottom 36×25×1.5=135036 \times 25 \times 1.5 = 135036×25×1.5=1350; two long walls 2×36×1.5×15=16202 \times 36 \times 1.5 \times 15 = 16202×36×1.5×15=1620; two short walls 2×22×1.5×15=9902 \times 22 \times 1.5 \times 15 = 9902×22×1.5×15=990; 1350+1620+990=39601350 + 1620 + 990 = 39601350+1620+990=3960 cm³ ✔.

  7. Answer 3960 cm³; 29.7 kg

    Common trap: Taking 3 cm off the height too — the box has no top.

  1. Hidden faces: the cone's base and the cylinder's top are joined; the closed bottom is outside.

  2. 1

    Cone height =52−32=4= \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4=52−32​=4 cm.

  3. 2

    TSA =π×3×5+2π×3×12+π×9=15π+72π+9π=96π=301.44= \pi \times 3 \times 5 + 2\pi \times 3 \times 12 + \pi \times 9 = 15\pi + 72\pi + 9\pi = 96\pi = 301.44=π×3×5+2π×3×12+π×9=15π+72π+9π=96π=301.44 cm².

  4. 3

    Volume =π×9×12+13π×9×4=108π+12π=120π=376.8= \pi \times 9 \times 12 + \dfrac{1}{3}\pi \times 9 \times 4 = 108\pi + 12\pi = 120\pi = 376.8=π×9×12+31​π×9×4=108π+12π=120π=376.8 cm³.

  5. Check: volume =πr2(12+43)=9π×403=120π= \pi r^2\left(12 + \dfrac{4}{3}\right) = 9\pi \times \dfrac{40}{3} = 120\pi=πr2(12+34​)=9π×340​=120π ✔.

    Note on the official key: the key gives the volume as 377.1 cm³. That is 120×227≈377.14120 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \approx 377.14120×722​≈377.14, found with π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​; the question says "Use π = 3.14", which gives 376.8 cm³. (The key's TSA, 301.44 cm², does use 3.14.)

    Common trap: Using the slant height 5 cm as the cone's height in the volume.

E28●● StandardShort answer · 2 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 12, Ex 12.4 Q10

500 persons are taking a dip into a cuboidal pond which is 80 m long and 50 m broad. What is the rise of water level in the pond, if the average displacement of the water by a person is 0.04m³?

π to use: none needed — no circles.

Full solution

Given: pond 80 m × 50 m; 500 people; 0.04 m³ each. Asked: the rise.

Concept used: water pushed up = base area × rise (Topic 5). Why it applies: the people take the place of 20 m³ of water.

  1. Hidden faces: none are joined — the people are in the water.

  2. 1

    Displaced =500×0.04=20= 500 \times 0.04 = 20=500×0.04=20 m³.

  3. 2

    Rise =2080×50=204000=0.005= \dfrac{20}{80 \times 50} = \dfrac{20}{4000} = 0.005=80×5020​=400020​=0.005 m =0.5= 0.5=0.5 cm.

  4. Check: 4000×0.005=204000 \times 0.005 = 204000×0.005=20 m³ ✔.

  5. Answer 0.5 cm

    Common trap: Giving 0.005 without the unit, or as cm.

E29●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 12, Ex 12.4 Q11

16 glass spheres each of radius 2 cm are packed into a cuboidal box of internal dimensions 16 cm × 8 cm × 8 cm and then the box is filled with water. Find the volume of water filled in the box.

π to use: 227\dfrac{22}{7}722​ (the Exemplar's rule).

Full solution

Given: box 16 × 8 × 8 (cm); 16 spheres of radius 2 cm. Asked: the water.

Concept used: water = box − spheres (Topic 5). Why it applies: the water fills the space the spheres leave.

  1. Hidden faces: none are joined — the spheres sit in the box (4 × 2 × 2 of them, each 4 cm wide, fill the box exactly).

  2. 1

    Box =16×8×8=1024= 16 \times 8 \times 8 = 1024=16×8×8=1024 cm³.

  3. 2

    One sphere =43×227×8=70421= \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 8 = \dfrac{704}{21}=34​×722​×8=21704​ cm³; sixteen =11 26421≈536.38= \dfrac{11\,264}{21} \approx 536.38=2111264​≈536.38 cm³.

  4. 3

    Water =1024−11 26421=10 24021≈487.62= 1024 - \dfrac{11\,264}{21} = \dfrac{10\,240}{21} \approx 487.62=1024−2111264​=2110240​≈487.62 cm³.

  5. Check: spheres fill π6\dfrac{\pi}{6}6π​ of the space round them: 1024×2242=11 264211024 \times \dfrac{22}{42} = \dfrac{11\,264}{21}1024×4222​=2111264​ ✔.

  6. Answer about 487.62 cm³ (the key: 487.6 cm³)

    Common trap: Using the diameter 4 cm as the radius.

E30●●● AdvancedShort answer · 4 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 12, Ex 12.3 Q8

Two solid cones A and B are placed in a cylinderical tube as shown in the Fig. 12.9. The ratio of their capacities are 2:1. Find the heights and capacities of cones. Also, find the volume of the remaining portion of the cylinder.

(Figure 12.9, described: a cylinder lying on its side, 21 cm long and 6 cm across; two cones fill its ends, their bases on the two end circles and their tips meeting at one point inside.)

π to use: 227\dfrac{22}{7}722​ (the Exemplar's rule).

Full solution

Given: cylinder length 21 cm, diameter 6 cm, so r=3r = 3r=3 cm; cones with bases on the ends and tips meeting; capacities 2 : 1. Asked: heights, capacities, the space left.

Concept used: cones with equal bases have volumes in the ratio of their heights; space = cylinder − both cones (Topics 4, 5). Why it applies: the two heights add up to 21 cm.

  1. Hidden faces: each cone's base lies on an end of the cylinder; the cones touch at their tips. The cylinder is the container.

  2. 1

    Heights in the ratio 2 : 1 and adding to 21 cm: 14 cm and 7 cm.

  3. 2

    Cone A =13×227×9×14=132= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 9 \times 14 = 132=31​×722​×9×14=132 cm³; cone B =13×227×9×7=66= \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 9 \times 7 = 66=31​×722​×9×7=66 cm³.

  4. 3

    Cylinder =227×9×21=594= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 9 \times 21 = 594=722​×9×21=594 cm³.

  5. 4

    Space left =594−132−66=396= 594 - 132 - 66 = 396=594−132−66=396 cm³.

  6. Check: the two cones together are a third of the cylinder (13×594=198=132+66\dfrac{1}{3} \times 594 = 198 = 132 + 6631​×594=198=132+66), so the space is 23×594=396\dfrac{2}{3} \times 594 = 39632​×594=396 ✔.

  7. Answer heights 14 cm and 7 cm; capacities 132 cm³ and 66 cm³; remaining 396 cm³

    Common trap: Splitting 21 cm equally.

C1 — Case: the adventure camp●● StandardCase/source-based · 4 marksCBSE Mathematics Class X Case Study Question Bank, Surface Areas and Volumes, Case Study 1

(Pictures, described: a cylindrical glass of diameter 7 cm and height 10.5 cm; a hemispherical cup of diameter 7 cm; a conical tent of base radius 7 m; a rectangle of canvas marked "Area = 551 m²".)

π to use: 227\dfrac{22}{7}722​ (the bank's answers use it; the case states no value).

Adventure camps are the perfect place for the children to practice decision making for themselves without parents and teachers guiding their every move. Some students of a school reached for adventure at Sakleshpur. At the camp, the waiters served some students with a welcome drink in a cylindrical glass and some students in a hemispherical cup whose dimensions are shown below. After that they went for a jungle trek. The jungle trek was enjoyable but tiring. As dusk fell, it was time to take shelter. Each group of four students was given a canvas of area 551m². Each group had to make a conical tent to accommodate all the four students. Assuming that all the stitching and wasting incurred while cutting, would amount to 1m², the students put the tents. The radius of the tent is 7m.

  1. The volume of cylindrical cup is

a) 295.75cm³ b) 7415.5cm³ c) 384.88cm³ d) 404.25cm³

  1. The volume of hemispherical cup is

a) 179.67cm³ b) 89.83 cm³ c) 172.25 cm³ d) 210.60 cm³

  1. Which container had more juice and by how much?

a) Hemispherical cup, 195 cm³ b) Cylindrical glass, 207 cm³ c) Hemispherical cup, 280.85 cm³ d) Cylindrical glass, 314.42 cm³

  1. The height of the conical tent prepared to accommodate four students is

a) 18m b) 10m c) 24m d) 14m

  1. How much space on the ground is occupied by each student in the conical tent

a) 54m² b) 38.5m² c) 86m² d) 24m²

Full solution

Given: glass r=3.5r = 3.5r=3.5 cm, h=10.5h = 10.5h=10.5 cm; cup r=3.5r = 3.5r=3.5 cm; canvas 551 m², 1 m² wasted; tent r=7r = 7r=7 m. Asked: five values.

Concept used: volumes of a cylinder and a hemisphere; CSA of a cone worked backwards; Pythagoras; area of a circle (Topic 1). Why it applies: each object is one basic solid.

  1. 1

    Part 1: 227×3.5×3.5×10.5=404.25\dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5 \times 10.5 = 404.25722​×3.5×3.5×10.5=404.25 cm³ → d).

  2. 2

    Part 2: 23×227×3.53≈89.83\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 3.5^3 \approx 89.8332​×722​×3.53≈89.83 cm³ → b).

  3. 3

    Part 3: the glass, by 404.25−89.83=314.42404.25 - 89.83 = 314.42404.25−89.83=314.42 cm³ → d).

  4. 4

    Part 4: canvas used =551−1=550= 551 - 1 = 550=551−1=550 m² =227×7×l=22l= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times l = 22l=722​×7×l=22l, so l=25l = 25l=25 m; height =252−72=576=24= \sqrt{25^2 - 7^2} = \sqrt{576} = 24=252−72​=576​=24 m → c).

  5. 5

    Part 5: floor =227×7×7=154= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154=722​×7×7=154 m²; each of 4 students =38.5= 38.5=38.5 m² → b).

  6. Check: Part 4: 227×7×25=550\dfrac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 25 = 550722​×7×25=550 ✔.

  7. Answer Part 1 d) · Part 2 b) · Part 3 d) · Part 4 c) · Part 5 b)

The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India, and an important monument of Indian Architecture. It was originally commissioned by the emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its nucleus was a simple hemispherical brick structure built over the relics of the Buddha. It is a perfect example of combination of solid figures. A big hemispherical dome with a cuboidal structure mounted on it. (Take π=227\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}π=722​)

  1. Calculate the volume of the hemispherical dome if the height of the dome is 21 m –

a) 19404 cu. m b) 2000 cu .m c) 15000 cu. m d) 19000 cu. m

  1. The formula to find the Volume of Sphere is-

a) 23πr3\dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^332​πr3 b) 43πr3\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^334​πr3 c) 4πr24\pi r^24πr2 d) 2πr22\pi r^22πr2

a) 1222 sq.m b) 1232 sq.m c) 1200 sq.m d) 1400 sq.m

a) 1344 sq. m b) 1232 sq. m c) 1392 sq.m d) 1932 sq. m

  1. The volume of the cuboidal shaped top is with dimensions mentioned in question 4

a) 182.45 m³ b) 282.45 m³ c) 292m³ d) 192m³

Full solution

Given: dome height 21 m (Part 1); dome radius 14 m and a cuboid 8 m × 6 m × 4 m on top (Parts 3–5). Asked: five values.

Concept used: a hemisphere's height is its radius; volume 23πr3\dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^332​πr3; CSA 2πr22\pi r^22πr2; hidden faces of a joined solid; cuboid volume (Topics 1, 2). Why it applies: the stupa is a dome with a cuboid on it.

  1. Hidden faces (Part 4): the cuboid's 8 m × 6 m base and the patch of the dome it sits on. The bank treats that patch of the dome as a flat 8 m × 6 m area (the top of a dome this large is nearly flat there), so both are taken away.

  2. 1

    Part 1: r=21r = 21r=21 m; 23×227×213=19 404\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21^3 = 19\,40432​×722​×213=19404 m³ → a).

  3. 2

    Part 2: the sphere's volume is 43πr3\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^334​πr3 → b).

  4. 3

    Part 3: 2×227×14×14=12322 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 = 12322×722​×14×14=1232 m² → b).

  5. 4

    Part 4: cuboid TSA =2(48+24+32)=208= 2(48 + 24 + 32) = 208=2(48+24+32)=208 m²; total =1232−48+208−48=1344= 1232 - 48 + 208 - 48 = 1344=1232−48+208−48=1344 m² → a).

  6. 5

    Part 5: 8×6×4=1928 \times 6 \times 4 = 1928×6×4=192 m³ → d).

  7. Check: Part 4 another way: the cuboid adds its four side faces and its top, 2(8+6)×4+48=1602(8 + 6) \times 4 + 48 = 1602(8+6)×4+48=160 m², and covers 48 m² of the dome: 1232+160−48=13441232 + 160 - 48 = 13441232+160−48=1344 ✔.

  8. Answer Part 1 a) · Part 2 b) · Part 3 b) · Part 4 a) · Part 5 d)

    Note on the official key: the bank's key (1 a, 2 b, 3 b, 4 a, 5 d) is correct. Part 4's 1344 m² takes away the patch of dome under the cuboid as if it were flat; option c) (1392 m²) would be the answer if that patch were not taken away.
